text.p: - Slovenia's electoral committee announced final official results of the country's second general election held on November 10. Liberal Democrats will get 25 seats in the 90-seat parliament, People's Party 19, Social Democrats 16, Christian Democrats 10, United List of Social Democrats nine, Pensioners' Party five and Nationalist Party four.
- Slovenia is among the first candidates for membership of NATO, a top NATO official said on Monday.
- Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek said he expects formal talks over putting together a new government to start soon.

- President of the conservative People's Party Marjan Podobnik expects the coalition government to be composed of rightist "Spring" parties and centre-left Liberal Democrats. "Spring" parties, which include the People's Party, Social Democrats and Christian Democrats, together won 45 out of 90 seats in parliament at the general election.
- Pharmaceutical producer Krka from southeastern Novo Mesto produces 13 out of 20 of the world's best-selling medicines.
- Foreign Minister Davorin Kracun and Defence Minister Jelko Kacin will participate in the ministerial meeting of the Western European Union in Belgium on Tuesday.
